IS:6053 (Part I)-1970

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR HAND TOOLS FOR FOOTWEAR INDUSTRY
PART I UPPER CLICKING KNIFE

0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 14 September 1970 after the draft finalized by the Footwear Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 In footwear industry clicking knives are used for cutting components out of leather or other materials in clicking operations. These knives have replaced the traditional method of clicking by scissors, which causes strain to the hands of user and does not give an accurate edge. Cutting with these knives give a quicker and efficient cutting. The knife is held between the palm and fingers to give maximum pressure on the knife while clicking. This provides one stroke-cut even for the heavy leather. If the adjustable blade of the knife is straightened up it may also cut lighter upper materials clearly. 0.3 The knife consists of a wooden handle, a hold-fast with adjustable screw arrangement, a metallic clamp and a steel blade. The curved steel blade is inserted to the hold-fast and clamped with wooden handle by means of the metallic clamp which helps in holding the knife during use. The curvature of the blade depends upon the thickness and type of the material to be cut; thicker the material more acute the curvature of the blade. 0.4 This standard contains clauses 4.1.2.1 and ment between the purchaser and the supplier. 6.1 which call for agree-

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ) .

SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements, methods of sampling and test for clicking knife used in `footwear industry for cutting of upper components of footwear. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definition shall apply. 2.1 Clicking Knife-A knife having a wooden or plastic handle with metallic sleeve which is tightened by screwing the handle holding the blade, known as extension blade. 3. TYPE 3.1 The upper clicking knives shall be of the following two types: Tyfie 1 -Upper clicking knife with adjustment the hand (see Fig. 1 ). Tyype 2 -Upper clicking (see Fig. 2). 4. REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Materials 4.1.1 Blades- The blades shall be made from either high carbon steel or low alloy steel or high speed steel and shall be of 0.6 mm thickness. 4.1.2 Handle-Handle of the clicking knife shall be made from wood which does not stain leather and conform generally to the requirements of Class V of IS : 620-1965*. 4.1.2.1 Handles manufactured from other suitable materials which do not cause stain to leather or break during use may also be used by agreement between the purchaser and the supplier.
NOTE The wood of Haldu ( Adina cordtjXia Hook. f. ) has also been found suitable.

4.1.4 Hold-fast, Cap and Ferrule-These shall be made from mild steel, In addition for Type 2 clicking having rust-preventive coating (see 8.2). knife, the ferrule and cap shall also be threaded. 4.2 Shape and Dimensions -The shape and dimensions of the clicking knife shall be as given in Fig. 1, and Fig. 2 for Type 2 clicking knives, respectively. 4.3 Hardness-The hardness of the finished steel blades measured near to the cutting edge as possible, when tested according IS: 1501-1968* shall be as given below: a) High carbon steel 693 to 762 HV b) Low alloy steel 762 to 840 HV c) High speed steel 738 to 840 HV

NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act, and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of.that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control during production. This system, which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as actually marketed are continuously checked by ISI for conformity to the standard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

8. TEST METHODS 8.1 The material shall be examined visually for all general requirements prescribed in 4.4. 8.2 The material used for handle, blade, hold-fast and screw shall be tested for the requirements given in 4.1 according to the relevant Indian Standard noted against them. Dimensions shall be checked by suitable callipers. 8.3 Test for Rust ProofnessClean or degrease the clamp, ferrule. or hold-fast selected for this purpose with benzene ( see IS : 1840-1961* ). Dip in a solution of copper sulphate (CuSOd, 5HzO; relative density l-17 at 27�C) for a duration of one minute and take out. Wash, wipe and dry with a clean soft cloth. Repeat the process of immersion and drying four times and examine visually. 8.3.1 To pass the test the clamp shall not show any sip red deposition bf copper after the fourth dip. of permanent

FOR CONFORMM'Y

A-2.1 All the selected clicking knives shall be examined for material, construction, dimensions and finish, and shall also be tested for sharpness (see 4.4.4 ). A knife failing in any one of the requirements given in 4.1, 4.2 The number of defectives shall not and 4.4 shall be taken as a defective. exceed the permissible number given in co1 3 of Table 1 if the lot is to be accepted as satisfactory. A-2.2 Two knives, if the lot size is 100 and below, and four knives ifthe lot size is above 100, shall be tested for the hardness of steel blade. There shall be ,no failures if the lot is to be accepted under this clause (see 4.3). For rust proofness of the cap, ferrule and hold-fast (see 4.1.4), two knives shall be tested and if both of them pass the test the lot shall be considered satisfactory in this regard.
